card.title: 13th ENGINEERS BATTALION
card.text: Gain an extra kredit slot when you deploy a unit with 3 or more operation cost.
card.flavorText: The 13th Engineer Battalion traces its lineage back to the American Civil War and has remained active throughout numerous conflicts until it was deactivated in 1994. During WWII, the 13th Engineer Battalion was brought back to action in California on July 8th, 1940. In 1943, they were sent along with elements of the 7th Infantry Division to the Aleutian Islands where they helped establish a beachhead at Massacre Bay in Alaska on May 11th, 1943. Later the battalion participated in the Battle of Attu Island, where they stopped a Japanese banzai charge, resulting in 239 enemy casualties. In 1944, they moved from Attu to Kwajalein Atoll, where they cleared out bunkers, shelters, and gun positions in just six days. Later that same year the battalion landed on Leyte where one of its units, Alpha Company, received a special award for their exceptional work in keeping the main supply route open under tough conditions. On April 1st, 1945, the 13th Engineer Battalion was part of the first group to land on Okinawa. There they took part in some of the toughest fighting of WWII, sealing up almost 600 caves and destroying others. In September they sailed with the 7th Infantry Division to Korea to accept the surrender of the Japanese forces there. From 1948 the 13th was stationed in Japan, until 1950 when it participated in the Korean War.
